title: Annotatio III §.II close: Augustine / Prosper ‘carried in His hands’; QUASI / QUODAMMODO; Picherellus; de Marca / Whitaker
pass_a_gloss: From the Latins it will have sufficed to have adduced these words of most eloquent AUGUSTINE, Serm. 1 on Ps. 33: Christ was being carried in His own hands, he says, when, commending His very body, He said: This is My Body; for He was bearing that body in His hands. Wholly parallel is the assertion of PROSPER OF AQUITAINE, De promiss. & prædicat. part 2 ch. 25: The Lord said, bearing His body in the sanctified bread with His hands: This is My body. These and other sayings of that flour, hyperbolically enough uttered by the Fathers — by which on one side they labored to amplify the mystery’s dignity, on the other to turn communicants from contemplating the outward symbols toward meditating the things signified more devoutly — some took too properly, not attending that the same Fathers not rarely softened their hyperboles by restrictive particles QUASI, QUODAMMODO and the like, as the most learned pontifical Author Peter Picherellus notes most accurately (Opusc. Theol. from p. 19 to the end). If anyone delights to read more hyperbolic expressions of the Fathers, it will not be in vain to unroll the celebrated Peter de Marca’s posthumous Dissertation on the Eucharistic Sacrament p. 15 — though drawn into pontifical use, i.e. abuse, and therefore vindicated by Blessed Whitaker, Tom. I p. 9.
pass_b_english: Augustine (Serm. 1 on Ps. 33): Christ was carried in His own hands when He said ‘This is My Body’; Prosper parallels Him bearing His body in the sanctified bread.
Such hyperboles aimed to exalt the mystery and turn communicants from outward symbols to the things signified — yet some took them too properly, missing QUASI / QUODAMMODO softenings (Picherellus).
More samples: de Marca’s posthumous Eucharist dissertation (pontifical abuse) — vindicated by Whitaker.
source_text: Ex Latinis, eloquentissimi AUGUSTINI verba hæcce adduxisse suffecerit Conc. 1. in Ps. 33. Ferebatur, inquit, Christus in manibus suis, quando, commendans ipsum corpus suum, ait: Hoc est Corpus meum; Ferebat enim illud corpus in manibus suis. Quibus omninò parallelum PROSPERI AQUITANICI de promis. & prædicat. part. 2. cap. 25. assertum: Dominus ait, suum corpus in sanctificato pane gestans manibus suis, dixit: Hoc est corpus meum. Hæc aliaque hujus farinæ Patrum hyperbolice satis enunciata, quibus una ex parte mysterii dignitatem amplificare atque extollere; Ex parte altera verò communicantes ab externorum symbolorum contemplatione ad res significatas tantò devotiùs meditandas convertere allaborarunt, nonnulli propriè nimis acceperunt, non attendentes, quibus iidem Patres hyperbolas suas haud rarò per restrictivas particulas QUASI, QUODAMMODO similesque, mitigarunt ac emolliverunt, annotante id ipsum perquam accuratè pontificio Autore eruditissimo Petro Picherello Opusc. Theol. à pag. 19. in fin. Si cui volupe est, plures Patrum hyperbolicas expressiones legere, haud frustra fuerit famigeratissimum Petrum de Marca Dissert. Posthuma de Euchar. Sacrament. p. 15. evolvere, quanquam in usum suum pontificium, i. e. abusum attractas, ideoque à B. Witakero vindicatas Tom. I. pag. 9.
